driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of 21 October 2026 after the GitHub Actions fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-10-20.json from Tuesday 20 October's close. Every figure used is dated at or before the 2026-10-20 close; the 2026-10-21 news-log entries were NOT used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched and were carried stale from the prior board (bonds TLT IV 15, 25 September; dollar EUR/USD 1M IV 4.72, 21 September; IWM RVX 19.97, 23 September). No newer prints were obtained.

News-log entries for 2026-10-20 (five) were confirmed identical to those in the Artifact database; no hand-entered issue entries were dated 20 October. Percentage changes are computed from the drafted 19 and 20 October closes. Cash-index levels, yields and oil come from the news log as written; no separate web search was run, to keep the blindness rule clean.

The Netflix Q3 report came after the 20 October close; its after-hours reaction is cited only as context for the Nasdaq-100 1-day earnings vote. The ZN close and the 10-year yield change point in slightly different directions (ZN -0.04%, yield -1.9bp), so rate-driven votes are neutral for bonds.
No 20 October high-yield OAS, MOVE, breadth count, positioning print, sentiment survey or seasonal statistic was obtained; those category votes are neutral.

newsLog.event: European equities opened lower for a second session as French unrest and fiscal worries widened the France-Germany 10-year spread to about 147bp; US 10-year Treasury yield held near 5.12% and US equity futures were flat to mixed ahead of another heavy earnings week (Netflix reports today).
newsLog.numbers: Euro Stoxx 50 -0.7%, DAX -0.7%, CAC 40 -0.3%, FTSE 100 -0.3%; FR-DE 10Y spread ~147bp; UST 10Y ~5.12%; S&P fut +0.1%, Nasdaq fut -0.2%
newsLog.reaction: Risk-off tone in Europe; US futures roughly flat with tech slightly weaker; long yields stay elevated near 5.1%.
newsLog.tickers: SPY, S&P, QQQ, Nasdaq, TLT, 10Y, yield, Treasury

newsLog.event: US stocks closed broadly higher led by the Dow as healthcare shares hit record highs; the Nasdaq slipped marginally on AI/debt-financing worries and ahead of this week's FOMC meeting. The 10-year Treasury yield held above 5.1%.
newsLog.reaction: Healthcare (XLV) hit an all-time high led by Eli Lilly; tech underperformed on AI/debt/high-rate worries (CoreWeave slid on data-center debt concerns, Meta fell a 5th straight session into earnings); major Asian indexes sold off led by Korea's Kospi.

newsLog.event: Netflix reported Q3 2026 results after the close: revenue was in line with its own forecast and operating margin beat on expense timing, but shares fell after the company cut full-year advertising-revenue and free-cash-flow guidance.
newsLog.numbers: Revenue $12.87B (+12% YoY); operating income $4.46B (+37%); operating margin 34.6% vs 28.2% y/y; net income $3.66B (+44%); diluted EPS $0.87 vs $0.59 y/y; buybacks $4.8B for 63.9M shares (largest quarter ever)
newsLog.reaction: Shares fell about 4.7% in after-hours/next-day trading to around $65 on the lowered ad and FCF guidance, overshadowing the margin beat and record buyback quarter.
newsLog.vsExp: Revenue in line with Netflix's internal forecast; operating margin came in above forecast; FY ad-revenue guidance cut to ~$2.7B from ~$3B and FY free cash flow cut to ~$12.0B from ~$12.5B

newsLog.event: General Motors beat Q3 profit estimates and announced a new $20B multi-year share buyback authorization, but shares fell as the company narrowed rather than raised its full-year profit outlook, which investors read as cautious.
newsLog.numbers: Revenue $50.0B (+2.9%); net income $3.3B vs $1.3B y/y; diluted EPS $3.73 vs $1.35 y/y; adjusted EPS $3.70 vs $2.80 y/y; EBIT-adjusted $4.1B (+21.6%); FY26 EBIT-adjusted guidance narrowed to $14.5-15.5B from $14.0-16.0B
newsLog.reaction: Shares fell about 7.8% intraday despite the earnings beat and new $20B buyback, as the narrowed (rather than raised) guidance range was taken as a cautious signal.
newsLog.vsExp: n/a (press release did not cite consensus estimates)

newsLog.event: September housing starts fell to a four-month low and missed expectations, while pending home sales also declined, as elevated mortgage rates continued to weigh on the housing market.
newsLog.numbers: Housing starts 1.221M SAAR (-5.9% m/m) vs 1.305M expected; pending home sales -7.3%
newsLog.reaction: Added to growth concerns alongside still-elevated mortgage rates; contributed to a cautious tone in rate-sensitive sectors ahead of the FOMC meeting.
